Naive de-embedding W_E @ W_enc[:, i] mixes 'what activates i' with 'what i pushes at output'.

Preserve the forward pass exactly, but linearize the backward pass.
→ gradient attribution becomes EXACT rather than a local approximation.
softmax is nonlinear. BUT if we FIX its
output p on a reference forward pass:
attn(V) = p · V ← linear in V
Same for LayerNorm: freeze the scale s,
then LN(x) = γ · (x/s) + β is linear in x.
Backward: real MLP gradient is DETACHED,
Any gradient through it is EXACT.

adjacency A (row-normalized) + top-logit weights w_L → compute each node's INFLUENCE:
I = (I + A + A² + A³ + …) · w_L = Σ_k Aᵏ · w_L
The graph is strictly layered (edges only early → late), so Aⁿ_layers = 0.
The sum is FINITE and EXACT - no truncation error, no approximation.

Fixed-position interventions only fire on the FIRST forward. For multi-token generation, wrap the position in a slice:
interventions = [(layer, slice(seq_len - 1, None, None), feat_idx, value)]
→ intervention fires at every generated token, not just the first.
"How much does source-node write into a direction that target-node reads,
given the model is linearized around this reference prompt?" Everything else is bookkeeping.
